init.description: The sensors below are optional: pick them and this charger receives their values automatically, every time they refresh in Home Assistant.

data.log_pushes: Log every value sent to the charger

data_description.car_soc_entity: Your car's state of charge. Sent to the charger whenever it changes and used by the "Use car SOC" constraint.
data_description.home_battery_soc_entity: Your home battery's state of charge. Required for the charger to accept any home battery data.
data_description.home_battery_power_entity: Your inverter's AC output power, or phase 1's on a three-phase inverter. Positive while the inverter injects, negative while it charges the battery, so pick a sensor that keeps the sign rather than an absolute value. It also sets the pace: the whole home battery set is sent every time this sensor refreshes, so the faster it polls the better the charger follows your surplus. The charger discards the data 60 seconds after the last one, so anything slower than that leaves gaps. Leave empty if you don't measure it, then the battery level sets the pace instead.
data_description.home_battery_invert_power: Turn on if your sensor reads negative while the inverter injects and positive while it draws. The charger expects the opposite: positive = injecting, negative = consuming. Check the log option below after switching it: with the sun up and the battery full, the power sent should be positive.
data_description.home_battery_voltage_entity: Your inverter's AC voltage. The charger divides the power above by it to get the current its solar logic runs on. Pick the grid/AC side, not a DC battery or string voltage: readings outside 50-300 V are ignored (so not 400 V line-to-line either). Without it only power is sent and solar charging cannot follow your surplus.
data_description.home_battery_phases: Pick 3 for a three-phase inverter. The next page then asks for the phase 2 and 3 sensors, and the two above count as phase 1. Each phase needs its own voltage: that is what tells the charger the phase is really there.
data_description.log_pushes: Troubleshooting only. Writes one line per send to Settings > System > Logs, so you can confirm what the charger receives. Leave off for normal use: with a fast inverter sensor this fills the log quickly.

phases.title: Three-phase inverter
phases.description: The sensors you already picked are phase 1. Add the other two phases here; each needs its own power and voltage, because a current only means anything per phase. Leave a phase empty if you don't measure it, the charger then treats the feed as single phase.

data_description.home_battery_power_entity_l2: Same sign convention and invert setting as phase 1.
data_description.home_battery_voltage_entity_l2: Phase-to-neutral voltage of phase 2, 50-300 V. Required for the charger to count phase 2 at all.
data_description.home_battery_power_entity_l3: Same sign convention and invert setting as phase 1.
data_description.home_battery_voltage_entity_l3: Phase-to-neutral voltage of phase 3, 50-300 V. Required for the charger to count phase 3 at all.

set_car_soc.name: Set car SOC
set_car_soc.description: Sends the car's state of charge to the charger, for use as a charge constraint. Stays valid for 24 hours.

soc.name: State of charge
soc.description: Car state of charge in percent.

set_home_battery_soc.name: Set home battery SOC
set_home_battery_soc.description: Sends the home battery state of charge, and optionally its current and power, to the charger for use by solar charge mode. The charger discards this after 60 seconds, so repeat at least that often.

soc.name: State of charge
soc.description: Home battery state of charge in percent.

amps.name: Inverter load current
amps.description: Signed phase 1 AC current in amps (i_ac): positive while injecting, negative while charging the battery. The charger treats anything below -2 A as no surplus for the car. Only send this if you measure current directly; otherwise send power and let the charger derive it. Omit if you don't measure it.

power.name: Inverter load power
power.description: Signed phase 1 AC power in watts (p_ac), same sign convention as the current. Omit if you don't measure it.

options.3: Three phase (a sensor pair per phase)
